title: Currency Symbols: Copy & Paste Money Signs & Symbols
meta_description: Browse and copy currency symbols, monetary signs, and financial Unicode characters from world currencies. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
hero_tagline: A reference collection of currency signs, monetary symbols, and financial Unicode characters. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: This library contains currency symbols from major world currencies, regional monetary signs, historical currency marks, and related financial Unicode characters. Symbols are organized by geographic region and usage.

sections.label: Complete Block Coverage
sections.h2: More from the Unicode Currency Symbols Block
sections.intro: Remaining assigned codepoints from the Unicode Currency Symbols block (U+20A0–U+20CF) not listed in the curated sections above.

paragraphs: Every sign on this page is a real Unicode codepoint, but most of the world's circulating currencies have none. Unicode does not invent currency signs: a central bank designs one and formally adopts it first, and most never have. That leaves three tiers.

Three currencies moved up a tier recently: the Saudi riyal sign (⃁ U+20C1) was finalized in Unicode 17.0, while the dirham sign (⃃ U+20C3) and Omani rial sign (⃄ U+20C4) became final in Unicode 18.0 on September 16, 2026. For the region's full tier-by-tier breakdown, see the Middle East currency symbol scorecard.
